Bozal Barril is herbaceous with notes of wet forest grass and anise. Additional flavors of agave, honey, and river stone, with a floral aftertaste.
Bozal Borrego is made in a similar fashion to a pechuga, however a leg of lamb (instead of a chicken breast) is used in the still.
Bozal Castilla is a special release made with maguey Castilla, a close relative of maguey Espadin. It's fruit forward with notes of wet earth.
Bozcal Cempasúchil is produced by adding Cempasúchil, a native Mexican flower, and mandarin peels to the final distillation
Bozal Cenizo has bright aromas of orange peel and floral notes. The palate has flavors of mesquite, barbecued meats, and dark chocolate.
Bozal Chino Verde has aromas of earth, dried herbs, and burlap with a soft smokiness. Ancho chiles are on the palate with flavors of charred meats.
Bozal Coyote is a clay pot distilled mezcal from Sola de Vega. The maguey Coyote is particularly rich in clay, which accentuates its delicate character.
Bozal Cuixe has rich green vegetal notes in the mouth and a dry smoky finish. It's made with wild maguey Cuixe.
Bozal Ensamble is made with cultivated maguey Espadin and wild maguey Barril and Mexicano. It's slightly smoky with lots of herbal tones.
Bozal Guias de Calabaza is made with Agave angustifolia in Rio de Ejutla, Oaxaca.

special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Espadin, Mexicano, Tobaziche; Pechuga
tasting_notes: Bozal Ibérico has a citrus-forward nose of lime and grapefruit with a tropical aroma of banana. It is viscous with a slight floral note of hibiscus flower
Bozal Jabali has notes of lavender and sage. It has bright green vegetal flavors of celery and parsley with a lingering finish of black pepper.
Bozal Madrecuishe has earthy flavors of beet and sweet potato along with minerality and hints of pollen.
Bozal Pechuga has a rich mouthfeel with flavors of roasted fruit, subtle minerality, and a slight smokiness, finishing dry on the back of the palate.
Bozal Sacatoro is made with agave Angustifolia that are cooked in an underground oven, milled by tahona, and fermented with open-air yeasts.
Bozal Tepeztate is distilled in small copper pot stills in the wild, mountainous region of Santa Ana del Rio, Oaxaca, which is home to other producers.
Bozal Tobala is bright and fresh with citrus and earthy flavors. It has aromas of ripe melon and apricots, and a finish of smoked tropical fruit.
Bozal Tobasiche has high minerality and an abnormally sweet nose. It's rather light on the palate with strong notes of anise.
Convite Coyote is produced traditionally with maguey Coyote in the beautiful Zapotec mountains of San Baltazar Guelavila, Oaxaca

special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Lumbre, Madrecuishe, Tepextate, Tobala, Tobaziche
tasting_notes: Convite Ensamble Silvestre is produced traditionally in the beautiful Zapotec mountains of San Baltazar Guelavila, Oaxaca
Convite Esencial is produced by mezcalero Cosme Hernández and his brother Daniel in the beautiful mountains of San Baltazar Guelavila, Oaxaca.
Convite Espadin-Madrecuishe is produced traditionally with maguey Espadin and maguey Madrecuishe in the beautiful mountains of San Baltazar Guelavila, Oaxaca
Convite Jabali is produced traditionally with agave Jabali in the beautiful Zapotec mountains of San Baltazar Guelavila, Oaxaca
Convite Tepextate is produced traditionally with agave Tepextate in the beautiful Zapotec mountains of San Baltazar Guelavila, Oaxaca
Convite Tobala is produced traditionally with maguey Tobala (agave potatorum) in the beautiful Zapotec mountains of San Baltazar Guelavila, Oaxaca
El Buho Arroqueño is made with maguey Arroqueño plants whose pinas weigh up to 300kgs when harvested after 15-25 years of growth.
El Buho Especial Cuishe is a limited release that is very hard to find. It is produced in Santiago Matatlan, Oaxaca with wild maguey Cuishe.

special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Arroqueño, Barril, Coyote, Cuishe; Especial
tasting_notes: El Buho Especial Ensamble is produced using wild agaves sourced in San Pablo Huixtepec, Oaxaca. This traditional ensamble is crafted from four different maguey species: Arroqueno, Coyote, Barril, and Cuishe.
El Buho Especial Jabali is a small-batch mezcal that has very limited releases. The first release of this was in 2017.
El Buho Especial Pulquero is produced by Octavio Jiménez Monterroza in Santiago Matatlan, Oaxaca using wild agave Atrovirens - the same plant that produces pulque.
El Buho Especial Tepeztate delivers an intense vegetal and earthen clay explosion of flavor with a long finish of agave, spice, and exotic green fruit.
El Buho Mezcal has notes of caramel, vanilla, salt, citrus, and dark chocolate. It's a good mixer and can be sipped neat.
El Buho Puro Capón has aromas of light pepper and sea shells, and tasting notes of burnt sugar, salt, and citrus.
El Buho Tobala-Espadin is the first ensamble released by El Buho as part of their black-bottle series, which is limited in production size.

special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Madrecuishe; mezcalero Juan Ramirez
tasting_notes: Gusto Historico Madrecuixe is produced by Juan Ramirez in the community of Miahuatlan, Oaxaca.
La Nina del Mezcal Espadin is made with estate-grown agave Expadin in Santiago Matatlan, which is known as the 'World Capital of Mezcal'
La Nina del Mezcal Madrecuixe is made with wild maguey Madrecuixe in Santiago Matatlan by mezcalero Armando Hernandez Lorenzo.
La Nina del Mezcal Pechuga is a small batch mezcal made in Santiago Matatlan, Oaxaca. Like most other Pechuga mezcals, this is triple distilled.
La Nina del Mezcal Primario is made specifically for use in cocktails. It has some light citric notes and a hint of smoke.

distillery: La Nina del Mezcal (CRM NOM O170X)
distillery_location: San Juan del Rio, Oaxaca, Mexico
tasting_notes: La Nina del Mezcal Tobala has sweet notes of tropical fruit, smoke, and charred berries. It's a delightful Tobala that is difficult to find in some regions.
Lalocura Cuishe is distilled in small clay pots in Santa Catarina Minas, Oaxaca. Like many mezcaleros, Lalo has been making mezcal for most of his life.
Lalocura Cuixe-Tepeztate is made by Eduardo 'Lalo' Angeles, who got his start alongside his father, the late, great Don Lorenzo of Real Minero.
Lalocura Espadin is made with agave Espadin. Lalo has been selling his mezcal in Oaxaca for years and it just became available in the US.

special_designation: Mezcal Ancestral; Espadin, Tobaziche; clay-pot; Pechuga
tasting_notes: Lalocura Pechuga is made by maestro mezcalero Eduardo “Lalo” Angeles, the son of the late, great Don Lorenzo of Real Minero.
Lalocura San Martinero is made in Santa Catarina Minas, which is home to some of the most talented clay-pot distillers in all of Mexico.
Lalocura Tepeztate is made by Eduardo Angeles, who got his start alongside his father, the late, great Don Lorenzo of Real Minero.
Lalocura Tobala is made by Eduardo 'Lalo' Angeles, the son of the late Don Lorenzo of Real Minero. Lalo learned to make mezcal from his father.
Lalocura Tobasiche is made by maestro mezcalero Eduardo 'Lalo' Angeles, who produces some of the most well-renowned mezcal in all of Oaxaca.
Lalocura Tobasiche-Espadin is made by maestro mezcalero Eduardo 'Lalo' Angeles, the son of the late, great Don Lorenzo of Real Minero.

special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Arroqueño; mezcalero Félix Ramírez Mendez
tasting_notes: Mal Bien Arroqueno from Félix Ramírez Mendez is produced in the village of Yogana, in the Ejutla district of Oaxaca.

distillery_location: Santa Maria La Pila, Oaxaca, Mexico
tasting_notes: Marca Negra Arroqueno is made by master Mezcalero Alberto Ortiz in very small batches that are typically limited to around 300 bottles.
Marca Negra Cupreata is a special edition mezcal that has been released at least twice, each time featuring a different producer.

distillery_location: Santa Maria La Pila, Oaxaca, Mexico
tasting_notes: Marca Negra Dobadan tastes of cooked agave with a touch of molasses and brown sugar, green herbs and grapefruit peel, a slight smoky to a sweet finish.

special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Bicuishe, Espadin, Madrecuishe, Mexicano, San Martinero
tasting_notes: Marca Negra Ensamble is made with several different types of agave. There are two different releases of this mezcal and both editions are worth trying.
Marca Negra Espadin has a fresh and clean aroma of ripe fruit. This Mezcal is moderately priced, and works well as a mixer or enjoyed neat.
Marca Negra Sanmartin is made with agave Sanmartin in La Noria Seccion 13, Ejutla, Oaxaca. It's clean on the nose with rich texture on the palate.

distillery_location: San Luis del Rio, Oaxaca, Mexico
tasting_notes: Marca Negra Sierra Negra is produced by Don Balta, who is known for his work with Alipus, Mezcalero, and other brands.

distillery_location: San Luis del Rio, Oaxaca, Mexico
tasting_notes: Marca Negra Tepeztate is produced in limited quantities due to the scarcity of the agave Tepeztate, which takes between 20-30 years to reach maturity.

distillery_location: San Luis del Rio, Oaxaca, Mexico
tasting_notes: The Marca Negra Tobala is a burly mezcal. As an maguey Tobala mezcal, the bar is high and Mezcal Marca Negra has made this a very complex spirit by making it with such high ABV.

distillery_location: San Juan del Rio, Oaxaca, Mexico
special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Tepextate, Tobala; mezcalero Joel Antonio Cruz
tasting_notes: Mezcalero No. 1 was made with wild maguey Tepeztate and Tobala from the distillery of Joel Antonio Cruz in San Juan del Rio.

distillery_location: San Juan del Rio, Oaxaca, Mexico
special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Sierra Negra; mezcalero Rodolfo Juan Juarez
tasting_notes: Mezcalero No. 10 is made from semi-wild maguey Sierra Negra. This special mezcal is made by distiller Rodolfo Juan Juarez in San Juan del Rio.

special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Bicuishe, Espadin, Madrecuishe, Mexicano; mezcalero Alberto Ortiz
tasting_notes: Mezcalero No. 11 is made with semi-wild maguey Madre-Cuishe, Bicuishe, and Mexicano, as well as cultivated Espadin. The body has notes of roasted meats.
Mezcalero No. 12 is made from agave Cupreata, which is very rarely distilled for export, yet it makes for a beautiful Mezcal.

distillery_location: San Luis del Rio, Oaxaca, Mexico
special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Tepextate, Tobala; mezcalero Luis Cruz
tasting_notes: Mezcalero No. 13 is made from maguey Tepeztate, which is known to be rich and spicy, and Tobalá, which has great elegance, complexity, and finesse.

special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Arroqueño; mezcalero Jesus Rios
tasting_notes: Mezcalero No. 14 is made from maguey Arroqueno, and the clay pot distillation that is used in production softens the Arroqueno's intensity.

distillery_location: San Luis del Rio, Oaxaca, Mexico
special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Sierra Negra; mezcalero Baltazar Cruz Gomez
tasting_notes: Mezcalero No. 15 was made with maguey Sierra Negra, which is notably suave, and carries an impressive flavor that is unsurpassed.

distillery_location: Santa Maria La Pila, Oaxaca, Mexico
special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Madrecuishe; mezcalero Valente Angel García
tasting_notes: Mezcalero No. 16 was made from maguey Madre-Cuishe. This is another beautifully distilled Mezcal from Don Valente Angel.

special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Espadin, Lumbre; mezcalero Cirilo Hernandez
tasting_notes: Mezcalero No. 17 was made from the wild and rare agave de Lumbre, which was blended at roasting with maguey Espadín. This mezcal is very round and mellow.

special_designation: Mezcal Ancestral; Arroqueño; clay-pot; mezcalero Jesus Rios
tasting_notes: Mezcalero No. 20 is a small-batch limited release made in the tiny town of El Potrero, near Sola de Vega, Oaxaca. Like all Mezcalero releases, this is a one-time bottling so grab a taste while you can.

distillery_location: San Luis del Rio, Oaxaca, Mexico
special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Cirial, Tepextate, Tobala; mezcalero Baltazar Cruz Gomez
tasting_notes: Mezcalero No. 21 was made by Don Baltazar Cruz, who is also responsible for Mezcalero No. 15, Mezcalero No. 19, and Alipus San Luis.

distillery_location: Santa Maria La Pila, Oaxaca, Mexico
special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Bicuishe; mezcalero Valente Angel García
tasting_notes: Mezcalero No. 22 was distilled in May 2015 by Don Valente Angel Garcia in Santa Maria la Pila, Miahuatlán, Oaxaca and rested for nearly 4 years.

special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Sierrudo; mezcalero Cirilo Hernandez
tasting_notes: Mezcalero No. 23 is made by Don Cosme Hernandez, who has not been bottled under the Mezcalero brand since Mezcalero No. 5.

distillery_location: San Luis del Rio, Oaxaca, Mexico
special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Espadin, Tepextate; mezcalero Baltazar Cruz Gomez
tasting_notes: Mezcalero No. 24 is an Ensamble of maguey Tepextate and maguey Espadin from San Luis del Rio. It was released in April 2020.

special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Tobala; mezcalero Cirilo Hernandez
tasting_notes: Mezcalero No. 25 was double distilled in a copper still before being aged in glass for six years before bottling.

distillery_location: Santa Maria La Pila, Oaxaca, Mexico
special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Arroqueño; mezcalero Valente Angel García
tasting_notes: Mezcalero No. 26 was distilled in April 2018 by Don Valente Angel Garcia in Santa Maria la Pila, Miahuatlán, Oaxaca.

distillery_location: San Juan del Rio, Oaxaca, Mexico
special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Espadin, Jabali, Tepextate; mezcalero Rodolfo Juan Juarez
tasting_notes: Mezcalero No. 27 was produced by mezcalero Rodolfo Juan Juarez in San Juan del Rio using Maguey Espadin, Tepextate, and Jabali.

distillery_location: Santa Maria La Pila, Oaxaca, Mexico
special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Bicuishe, Espadin, Madrecuishe, Mexicano; mezcalero Valente Angel García
tasting_notes: Mezcalero No. 28 was distilled in May 2013 by Don Valente Angel Garcia in Santa Maria la Pila, Miahuatlán, Oaxaca.

special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Tepextate; mezcalero Octavio Jiménez Monterroza
tasting_notes: Mezcalero No. 29 is a limited release of wild maguey Tepextate from Octavio Jiménez in Santiago Matatlan, Oaxaca.

distillery_location: Santa Maria La Pila, Oaxaca, Mexico
special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Espadin, Mexicano; mezcalero Valente Angel García
tasting_notes: Mezcalero No. 3 was made with wild maguey Mexicano and cultivated maguey Espadin by Don Valente Angel in Santa Maria la Pila.

special_designation: Mezcal Ancestral; Arroqueño; clay-pot; mezcalero Felix Garcia
tasting_notes: Mezcalero No. 9 was made with semi-wild maguey Arroqueño from three neighboring clay-pot distilleries in Potrero de Sola de Vega.

special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Madrecuishe; mezcalero Alberto Ortiz
tasting_notes: Mezcalero Special Bottling No. 1 rested in a tank for 18 months following distillation. The calm resting makes this smooth and fruity.

distillery_location: Santa Maria La Pila, Oaxaca, Mexico
special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Mexicano; mezcalero Valente Angel García
tasting_notes: The label of Mezcalero Special Bottling No. 2 states that it is the 'Finest Mezcal in Bottle,' and many will argue that this is true.

distillery_location: San Juan del Rio, Oaxaca, Mexico
special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Tobala; mezcalero Rodolfo Juan Juarez
tasting_notes: Mezcalero Special Bottling No. 3 is a limited release made with wild maguey Tobala. This mezcal was rested 2 years before bottling.

distillery_location: Santa Maria La Pila, Oaxaca, Mexico
special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Bicuishe, Espadin; mezcalero Valente Angel García
tasting_notes: Mezcalero Special Bottling No. 4: De Cabra was aged in glass for six months, using a rather unusual environment to store the aging mezcal.
Mezcalero Special Bottling No. 5 is distilled in Durango by mezcalero Don Rubén Solis Lozano from wild Cenizo (Agave durangensis).

distillery_location: San Juan del Rio, Oaxaca, Mexico
special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Azul; mezcalero Rodolfo Juan Juarez
tasting_notes: Mezcalero Special Bottling No. 6 was made by Don Rodulfo Juan Juarez. It was produced using maguey Azul in San Juan del Rio, Oaxaca.

special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Bicuishe, Madrecuishe, Tobala; mezcalero Margarito Cortés
tasting_notes: Mezcalosfera Bicuishe / Tobala / Madrecuishe was produced by maestro mezcalero Margarito Cortés, who has been producing mezcal in Miahuatlan for many years.

special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Bicuishe, Madrecuishe, Verde; mezcalero Emanuel Ramos
tasting_notes: Mezcalosfera Bicuixe/Madrecuixe/Verde was produced in Miahuatlan, Oaxaca in June 2017 and released in the US in December 2017.

special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Espadin; Pechuga; mezcalero Margarito Cortés
tasting_notes: Mezcalosfera con Mango y Chile Habanero is a small-batch traditional mezcal that was released at the same time as the Espadin con Cacao.

special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Espadin; Pechuga; mezcalero Job Cortés
tasting_notes: Mezcalosfera con Mango y Chile Habanero is made by Job Cortes, who comes from a family that has been producing traditional mezcal for many generations.

special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Espadin; Pechuga; mezcalero Margarito Cortés; con Cacao
tasting_notes: Mezcalosfera Espadin con Cacao is a small-batch traditional mezcal that was released at the same time as the Espadin con mango y chile habanero.

special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Espadin; Pechuga; mezcalero Margarito Cortés; con Café
tasting_notes: Mezcalosfera Espadin con Cafe is made by mezcalero Margarito Cortes who is known for experimenting with additional ingredients in a third distillation - in this mezcal he adds coffee.

special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Espadin, Jabali; mezcalero Victor Ramos
tasting_notes: Mezcalosfera Espadin/Jabali is produced by mezcalero Victor Ramos in Miahuatlán, Oaxaca; it was adjusted to a final ABV of 47.71% using puntas and shishe.

special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Madrecuishe; mezcalero Margarito Cortés
tasting_notes: Mezcalosfera Madrecuixe is made with wild maguey Madrecuixe. This was the first single varietal Mezcalosfera available in the US.

special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Bicuishe, Madrecuishe, Tepextate, Tobaziche; mezcalero Emanuel Ramos
tasting_notes: Mezcalosfera Madrecuixe/Bicuixe/Tobaxiche/Tepextate is the 3rd mezcal from Mezcaloteca to be imported into the United States. Like the others, it's rare.

special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Tobaziche; mezcalero Emanuel Ramos
tasting_notes: Mezcalosfera Maguey Tobasiche is made in Miahuatlan, an area well-known for its production of karwinksii agave, like Tobasiche.

special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Madrecuishe, Tobala; mezcalero Felipe Cortés
tasting_notes: Mezcalosfera de Mezcaloteca Tobala/Madrecuixe is an incredibly elegant Ensamble of two distinct agaves. This is the first US release from Mezcalosfera de Mezcaloteca.

special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Cuishe, Espadin, Madrecuishe, Tobala, Verde; mezcalero Felipe Cortés
tasting_notes: Mezcalosfera Tobala/Verde/Madrecuixe/Cuixe/Espadin is a rare mezcal that is hard to find. It's a complex offering that keeps you wanting more.

special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Cuishe, Espadin, Jabali, Mexicano; mezcalero Alejandrina Aragón Hernandez
tasting_notes: Rezpiral Jabali, Mexicano, Espadin, Cuishe is produced by Alejandrina & Nicolas Hernandez in a valley outside of Santa Maria Zoquitlán

special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Tepextate; mezcalero Alejandrina Aragón Hernandez
tasting_notes: Rezpiral Tepeztate is produced by Alejandrina & Nicolas Hernandez in a valley outside of Santa Maria Zoquitlán

special_designation: Mezcal Artesanal; Tepextate, Tobala; mezcalero Berta Vasquez
tasting_notes: Rezpiral Tobala / Tepeztate from Berta Vasquez is produced by famed maestra mezcalera Berta Vasquez in San Baltazar Chichicapam, Oaxaca.
Siete Misterios Arroqueno is produced with maguey Arroqueno that are milled entirely by hand and distilled in small clay pots.
Siete Misterios Barril is made with 100% maguey Barril, which is named for its resemblance to a barrel once the leaves are cut to prepare for cooking.
Siete Misterios Coyote mezcal is very rare and hard to find, due to the rarity of the maguey Coyote in the Sola de Vega region. If you see it, try it.

distillery_location: San Luis del Rio, Oaxaca, Mexico
tasting_notes: Siete Misterios Doba-Lá is made from maguey Tobalá (Agave Potatorum). 'Doba-Lá' is the Zapotec name for maguey Tobalá.
Siete Misterios Doba-Yej is the first expression from Siete Misterios that is made in a copper still, and produced outside the region of Sola de Vega.
Siete Misterios Espadin is hand milled and distilled in a clay pot still. There are not many other clay pot distilled Espadin mezcals currently available.
Siete Misterios Espadin/Mexicanito Ensamble was produced in San Dionisio Ocotepec, Oaxaca.
Siete Misterios Mexicano is the most rare of their releases. They only produce about 200 bottles of this each year, so make sure to try it if you see it.
Siete Misterios Pechuga is one of their more rare releases. They produce less than 500 litres of this per year, making it somewhat hard to find.
Siete Misterios Tobala has full flavor characteristics that jump around the palate. Given the small size of the maguey Tobala, this is a unique release.
Tosba Arroqueno is made by Edgar Gonzalez, who comes from several generations of sugar cane aguardiente producers in San Cristóbal Lachirioag.
Tosba Cenizo Mezcal is a unique release because Agave durangensis is not native to the state of Oaxaca where Mezcal Tosba is produced.
Mezcal Tosba Espadilla is produced by mezcalero Edgar Gonzalez Ramirez in San Cristobal Lachirioag, Oaxaca.
Tosba Espadin has a light nose with a long-lasting citrus and fruitiness on the tongue. It's good to enjoy neat, and also makes a great cocktail.
Tosba Pechuga is a double distilled Mezcal that uses a combination of wild pineapple, bananas, wild apples, rice, and a wild turkey breast.
Tosba Pechuga de Borrego is an special batch of Tosba Pechuga made with lamb breast; it honors the wedding between the founders of Tahona Mercado and is exclusive to their shops.
Tosba Tepextate is made with agave Tepextate that is grown among cultivated coffee trees, sugar cane, mango, and other fruit trees.
Tosba Tobala has a sweet and fruity nose. The Tobala is a much smaller agave than the Espadin and it can be harder to cultivate.
Tosba Warash is a limited release that is fruit forward with rounded notes of grilled pineapple and other sweet tropical fruit.
